fixed_before_run: This file is committed before the first data fetch. A change after that needs a new commit and a new run, and both are recorded in the output manifest.
role: Context only. Weather is shown beside the fire comparison. It is never used in the harmonised record, the anomaly classes or any score, and it is never presented as the cause of fire.

source.name: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources), Daily API
source.note: Meteorology from GMAO MERRA-2, extended towards near real time by GEOS-IT (the POWER answer header lists MERRA2, GEOSIT and POWER), on a 0.5 x 0.625 degree grid. No key is needed.

period.end: the latest UTC day for which every point has a value, and no later than 3 days before the fetch

area.grid: 3 x 3 points per preset box: the centres of the nine equal parts of the box
area.value: the mean of the nine points for each day and parameter
area.missing: if any of the nine points has no value for a day and parameter, that day is missing for that parameter. Missing stays missing and is never filled

comparison.dates: the same dates as 'Now against the past': the chosen window, and the same calendar dates in every other year
comparison.window_value: rain: total over the window in mm (sum of the daily mm/day values). Other parameters: mean of the daily values
comparison.complete: a year is used only if every day of its window has a value
comparison.rain_before: rain total over the 60 days that end the day before the window starts, compared the same way
comparison.normal: median over the same baseline years the fire comparison uses, the chosen year left out, only if at least 10 years are usable
comparison.rank: rank of the chosen year among all usable years including itself. 1 = the driest (rain, humidity, soil wetness) or the hottest or windiest (maximum temperature, wind)
comparison.shown_as: rain, rain before, wind and soil wetness as percent of the normal. Humidity as a difference in percentage points. Maximum temperature as a difference in degrees C
comparison.provisional: a window that includes any day in the 120 days before the fetch is labelled provisional, because near-real-time values can be revised
